text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, the best pick is a 250-500 Wh station, since weight and simplicity matter more than capacity. If you need a fridge or multi-day power, step up to about 1 kWh or more.

## Compact picks (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288 Wh, 8.3 lb, 300 W) is PowerStationGearLab's best overall for camping. Jackery's own US site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so you'd buy the Plus from Amazon or other retailers. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288 Wh, 5-year warranty) has a built-in lantern and is often the cheapest 288 Wh LiFePO4 unit. Make sure you get the standard C300 with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC" variant. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286 Wh, 600 W inverter) is expandable to 572 Wh. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268 Wh, 600 W) is the budget option. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

Reviewers disagree on the small units. OutdoorGearLab scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low in its tests, though it still rates the Jackery 300 its best buy for phones and laptops. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Bigger picks (fridge, electric cooler, multi-day trips)
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, ~16 kg, 5-year warranty) lists at $499. [Buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). Dealectric says code AFF5OFF takes $24.95 off, bringing it to $474.05. That's an affiliate site that earns a commission, and the store's checkout has the final word on price. The $499 is for the station alone, and it has no expansion port. [Source](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. It's 25 lb, with 890 Wh measured, and was on sale for under $530. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It's 39 lb and 2,042 Wh, listed at $1,499 and recently under $900 on Amazon. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's best for camping. It's IP65-rated, about 40 lb, and 1,536 Wh, at roughly $1,079-1,199. [Source](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Quick sizing
A phone charge takes about 10 Wh, a CPAP night 30-60 Wh (turn the humidifier off), and a camp lantern about 5 Wh per night. A 288 Wh unit covers a weekend of that. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## My pick
- **Tent or car camping with small electronics:** Anker SOLIX C300 or Jackery 300 Plus.
- **Running a cooler or fridge, or camping for several days:** Bluetti AC180 or Anker C1000 Gen 2.

The search results gave me direct buy links only for the Bluetti AC180. For the others, the review pages above have the retailer buttons, and prices change, so check the current price before buying.

If you tell me your budget and what you'll power, I can narrow this to one.
